original_title: What Should You Watch This Weekend? (August 7-9)
summary_en: Dive into the dark, debauched world of 1980s Los Angeles with FX's adaptation of Bret Easton Ellis's acclaimed novel. Plus, the epic conclusion of a literary masterpiece arrives on Netflix.

en.title: Ryan Murphy's 'The Shards' Series Drops: What to Watch This Weekend
en.summary: Dive into the dark, debauched world of 1980s Los Angeles with FX's adaptation of Bret Easton Ellis's acclaimed novel. Plus, the epic conclusion of a literary masterpiece arrives on Netflix.
en.body:
This weekend, the screen beckons with a blend of stylish adaptation and sweeping literary grandeur. FX is rolling out **Ryan Murphy**’s highly anticipated series, **The Shards**, bringing Bret Easton Ellis's 2022 novel to life. Set against the neon-drenched, privileged backdrop of 1980s Los Angeles, the story centers on a group of teenagers whose lives are shattered by the arrival of a mysterious killer. While early buzz suggests the series might lean into a more operatic, soapier tone than the book's unflinching darkness, the formidable talent involved, including a strong cast and FX's reputation for quality, signals a must-watch event for fans of the author and stylish thrillers. The network's commitment indicates they're investing in this for the long haul, making now the perfect time to jump in, whether you're a seasoned reader of Ellis or new to his provocative worlds.

Beyond the glitz of LA, a monumental literary achievement reaches its next chapter. Netflix is releasing the second part of its ambitious adaptation of Gabriel García Márquez’s **One Hundred Years of Solitude**. This sprawling, 16-episode Spanish-language series tackles one of the 20th century's most celebrated novels, charting the multi-generational saga of the Buendía family in the mythical town of Macondo. The first half of the series, released in 2024, covered the initial 50 years of the epic tale. Now, seven new episodes are dropping, with a feature-length finale promised to conclude the adaptation. For anyone who has ever been captivated by magical realism or the sheer scope of Márquez's storytelling, this is an unmissable continuation.

## Thrills and Wilderness Adventures Await

For those seeking more immediate thrills, the espionage thriller **Lioness**, created by **Taylor Sheridan**, returns for its third season on Paramount+. Starring **Zoe Saldaña**, the series continues its high-octane international espionage. If you’ve fallen off the wagon, Saldaña’s compelling presence is always a reason to tune back in. Meanwhile, USA Network is launching a new park ranger mystery series based on **Nevada Barr**'s beloved Anna Pigeon novels. If your idea of a perfect mystery involves rugged wilderness and remote investigations, this series promises to deliver scenic thrills and intriguing puzzles.

## A Quiet Weekend for New Films

Movie night options among new releases appear somewhat scarce this weekend, with Hollywood seemingly pushing audiences back to theaters for blockbusters like **The Odyssey** and **Spider-Man**. For those staying home, however, the streaming landscape offers a chilling independent film titled **Yeti** – a perfect pick for those craving a unique genre experience. While the big screen may be dominated by tentpoles, the small screen and streaming services continue to offer diverse content for every taste, from literary adaptations to genre-specific thrills.

## What's Next

As August unfolds, expect more compelling book-to-screen adaptations and new literary fiction to hit the shelves. Keep an eye on releases like **Lisa Gardner**'s spooky thriller **You'll Be Sorry** and **Tarah DeWitt**'s romance novel **Lost and Found**, which are set to captivate readers looking for their next great read.

content_raw: A mystery lover’s guide to what’s new to streaming this weekend. ___________________________________ New and Returning Mystery and Thriller Series __________________________________ The Shards (FX) From Ryan Murphy and FX, this is the splashy new adaptation of Bret Easton Ellis’ recent novel about a killer stalking the privileged, debauched youth of 1980s LA. The book was dark and fantastic; the show looks a little soapier than maybe some were expecting, but there’s no doubt that the A-team at FX has been called in for this one, with a strong cast and a lot of strong buzz surrounding the premiere. FX is signaling that it’s in it for the long haul with The Shards , so better to start in with it now and take the ride. And if you haven’t read the book yet, it’s as good a time as any to pick that up, too. Lioness, season 3 (Paramount+) Zoe Saldaña is still out there doing international espionage in this blow ’em up Taylor Sheridan created adrenaline kick. You may have been in on season one and since lost track of the show. I may have done that, is what I mean. But Zoe Saldaña is always worth watching. Anna Pigeon (USA) The new team at USA is kicking things off with their version of a park ranger mystery. This one’s based on the Nevada Barr novels. If you’re in the mood for some wilderness investigations, this is your next stop. ___________________________________ Movie Night ___________________________________ For movies, your options among the newer selections are pretty scarce again this weekend. Everyone’s still going to the theaters to see The Odyssey , plus now Spiderman . Hollywood doesn’t want you at home. But if you’re couch-bound and, say, re-sleep training your sleep-regressed baby (yes, I messed that up, but I’m going to fix it…), you’re going to need some streaming options, so I’m here for you. On the one hand, you could try Pressure (Peacock), the new movie about how weather projections with the D-Day invasion hanging in the balance. Yes, that’s right, I said weather projections. Kind of a cool angle, right? Or you could give The Sheep Detectives (Prime) a shot. This is the one with Hugh Jackman and a bunch of sheep that talk. I’ll be honest, there’ s no chance in hell I’m going to watch The Sheep Detectives , but my wife saw the trailer at the theater a while back and for some reason it absolutely cracked her up and every once in a while she’ll still mention those two minutes and how funny they were. That’s got to mean something, right? Plus 5 new additions to the libraries… Erin Brockovich (2000) (Tubi) Widows (2018) (Tubi) The Presidio (Pluto) The Thomas Crown Affair (1968) and (1999) (Prime)
